summary: Configured pam_pwquality on node1 (AlmaLinux 9) to require new passwords of at least 12 characters and at least 3 character classes (minlen=12, minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf). Confirmed enforcement via real non-root user password-change tests both pre- and post-restart (weak passwords rejected, compliant passwords accepted). Restarted node1 with verified boot-identity change and confirmed policy persisted. All test users cleaned up.
actions_performed: Inspected existing pwquality.conf and confirmed pam_pwquality.so is already wired into /etc/pam.d/system-auth and /etc/pam.d/password-auth
Backed up pwquality.conf, then set minlen=12 and minclass=3
Discovered root-initiated `passwd <user>` bypasses pwquality checks (expected PAM behavior for privileged callers), so re-tested policy as the actual unprivileged user changing their own password
Verified: 7-char password rejected, 14-char single-class password rejected, 12-char 3-class password accepted (tested as a real, non-root user)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and baseline config state
Triggered `shutdown -r now` via nohup/background so the exec acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec was reachable again
Confirmed boot_id changed from 15443601-befc-4fc4-aa76-b417968ad3f9 to 719c426a-5189-4b49-9f9c-fe7b5cb67e5b and uptime reset to 0, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified pwquality.conf values and PAM wiring post-restart
Re-ran the weak/strong password functional test as a real user post-restart, confirming the policy persisted across reboot
Removed all temporary test users created during testing (pwtestuser, pwtestuser2, pwtestuser3, pwtestuser4)

evidence.requirement: minlen=12 and minclass=3 configured in pwquality.conf, with pam_pwquality wired into PAM stack
evidence.summary: pwquality.conf updated to minlen=12, minclass=3 (backed up original first); pam_pwquality.so confirmed present with requisite control in both system-auth and password-auth

evidence.requirement: Policy actually enforced for real (non-root) user password changes, pre-restart
evidence.summary: As pwtestuser3 changing their own password: [REDACTED] password rejected (exit 1), 14-char single-class password rejected (exit 1), 12-char 3-class password accepted (exit 0)
Pre-restart boot_id=15443601-befc-4fc4-aa76-b417968ad3f9 captured along with confirmed pwquality.conf values and PAM wiring
Background `shutdown -r now` dispatched; exec stream closed as expected once reboot proceeded, confirming the command was accepted and executing

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Node unreachable immediately after reboot (connection timed out), then reachable again with boot_id=719c426a-5189-4b49-9f9c-fe7b5cb67e5b (changed from baseline) and uptime reset to 0 minutes

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required configuration and functional enforcement
evidence.summary: pwquality.conf still shows minlen=12/minclass=3, PAM wiring intact, and live test as pwtestuser4 confirms weak password rejected (exit 1) and compliant password accepted (exit 0); test user removed afterward

evidence.requirement: Test artifacts cleaned up, no residual state left on node1
evidence.summary: All temporary test users (pwtestuser2/3/4) removed and confirmed absent via `id` lookups
